Article Title: The Surat link to US fentanyl crisis
Article Text:
Just 2mg of fentanyl — an amount that can fit on a pencil tip — is enough to kill an adult. In Dec 2025, the latest month for which full data is available, over 70,000 drug overdose deaths occurred in US, with authorities saying that “approximately 69% of all overdose deaths involved synthetic opioids, overwhelmingly illicitly made fentanyl and its analogues”

The Surat files

Chinese, Afghan trigger

Regulatory route

With inputs from Parag Dave

It takes only two milligrams of fentanyl, an amount that can fit on the tip of a pencil, to kill an adult, according to the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). Fifty times more potent than heroin and 100 times more potent than morphine, fentanyl has become the leading cause of accidental death among Americans aged 18 to 44. The scale of the crisis is reflected in the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s July release, which noted that “approximately 69% of all overdose deaths involved synthetic opioids, overwhelmingly illicitly made fentanyl and its analogues”.As US cracks down on illicit fentanyl use, the ripples have reached the distant shores of India’s western coast. Enforcement action has extended to entities linked to the chemicals and pharmaceuticals hub of Surat, with India being seen as filling a supply void created by China’s strict ban on the key ingredients that go into fentanyl production.Yet fentanyl itself is not an illicit drug. Legally manufactured fentanyl is essential to modern medicine, with uses ranging from severe pain management and cancer care to anaesthesia and trauma treatment. It is tightly controlled in the US and regulated under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act in India. India’s regulatory framework, however, has been exploited by illicit actors sourcing chemicals for fentanyl production.A Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad’s case from 2025 centres on Satishkumar Sutaria of Surat-based Athos Chemicals. Investigators allege that Sutaria and associate Yukta Modi, now out on bail, forged end-user certificates — the mandatory declarations designed to ensure dual-use chemicals reach legitimate buyers — to obtain huge quantities of chemicals that go into to the making of fentanyl.According to investigators, chemicals like N-Boc-4-piperidone, 4-Anilino-N-phenethylpiperidine (ANPP), and N-Phenethyl-4-piperidone were routed to J&C Import, a Guatemalan company allegedly linked to Mexican drug trafficking cartel Sinaloa intermediary Jaime Augusto Barrientos Camaz. One kilogram of N-Boc-4-piperidone can yield about 1.8kg of fentanyl, enough for about 9 lakh lethal doses. Sutaria and Modi are accused of facilitating, among other things, the procurement of 116kg of N-Boc-4-piperidone. This April, the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed sanctions on Sutaria, Modi, and their associated companies. But the Indian links don’t end there.A US federal case in Brooklyn has implicated another Surat businessman, Bhavesh Lathia of Raxuter Chemicals, who pleaded guilty to distributing and smuggling more than 50 pounds of precursor chemicals. Prosecutors said he brokered sales online and knowingly mislabelled shipments as “Vitamin C” and “antacids” to slip past customs. He faces up to 40 years in prison.For years, Mexican cartels sourced many of its precursor chemicals through China. But, investigators say, procurement networks increasingly turned to India as Beijing tightened controls.Enforcement attention on Gujarat is explained by its position in India’s chemicals trade. The state accounts for roughly 50% of the country’s chemical output across more than 5,000 chemical units. It is also home to around 3,000 pharmaceutical units. Deep-water ports such as Mundra and Pipavav provide direct maritime access to Central America, with India’s roughly $60-billion pharma industry one of the world’s largest such ecosystems.It is this ecosystem that unscrupulous actors have used to drive illegal sales. “Customers may operate through intermediaries, distributors, brokers, or multiple business entities. Documentation may appear complete, yet the actual end-use of a chemical may not always be fully transparent,” said Dr Jaimin Vasa, president of Gujarat Chemical Association. What raises red flags, he added, are “unusually large orders, purchase quantities inconsistent with declared business activities, unusual urgency or unconventional payment arrangements”.The US Intelligence Community’s 2025 Annual Threat Assessment ranks India second only to China as a source of illicit fentanyl precursors and pill-pressing equipment. But the trail is complex. The 2025 annual report of International Narcotics Control Board (INCB) logged four European seizures of 1-Boc-4-piperidone in the second half of 2024, noting that “the substance originated in India”.India responded in Jan 2025, bringing two fentanyl precursors, including 1-Boc-4-piperidone, under stricter control through Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Amendment Order, 2025. The payoff was measurable: a coordinated interdiction using INCB’s pre-export notification online system stopped three tonnes of the chemical from reaching illicit channels. The board estimated that the shipment could have produced 1.4 to 3.3 tonnes of fentanyl, or somewhere between 700 million and 1.6 billion potentially lethal doses.The geography of the trade changed dramatically on May 1, 2019, when China imposed class-wide controls on finished fentanyl-related substances or analogues.The significance lay in the method. Rather than banning substances one by one, China’s 2019 framework covers any compound that meets defined structural criteria — including variants not yet seen on the market. That closed the traffickers’ oldest workaround: altering the finished fentanyl molecule just enough to produce a potent but unregulated analogue.Shut out at the finished-drug end, syndicates moved further back down the synthesis chain. Rather than modifying the drug, rogue suppliers began modifying precursor building blocks (pre-precursors) such as para-fluoro-Boc-4-AP and ortho-methyl-Boc-4-AP (BOC-X) — chemicals that passed customs screening lawfully while still serving as effective inputs for the production of fentanyl and fentanyl analogues.In mid-2024, China tightened controls further, placing 24 precursor chemicals under export licensing requirements. On July 20, 2025, Beijing brought 4-piperidone and 1-Boc-4-piperidone under strict national control.Did it work? Researchers Chao Wang and Nicholas Lassi of Zhejiang University’s Guanghua Law School argue it displaced the problem rather than dismantling it. In “Combating illicit fentanyl: Will increased Chinese regulation generate a public health crisis in India?”, they trace how sourcing migrated — citing DEA intelligence that syndicates moved precursor procurement from China to India between Feb and March 2018, “likely due in part to China’s regulation of ANPP and NPP”.A second shock reshaped the market at the same time. The Taliban’s ban on opium poppy cultivation drove a 95% collapse in Afghan opium production, according to INCB, pushing demand harder towards synthetics. INCB has since flagged the arrival of nitazenes — opioids up to 30 times more potent than fentanyl, now being sold as “synthetic heroin”.Precursor control is where the two Asian giants take different paths. China regulates by chemical class. India regulates by list — naming substances one by one, which means regulators must identify each new compound after traffickers have already begun using it.India has been expanding that list fast. On Jan 23, 2025, the department of revenue added 18 designer compounds under Schedule B and C controls, including 4-piperidone, 1-Boc-4-piperidone. As of June 1, 2026, the national precursor registry covers 46 scheduled substances. Scheduled substances are those whose production and use is tightly controlled to prevent misuse.But the hardest chemicals to control are the ones legitimate industry cannot function without. Aniline and propionyl chloride — both associated with the Gupta synthesis pathway (see box) — are widely used in India’s dye, rubber and textile sectors, and remain unscheduled for that reason.In June 2026, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) responded by introducing a Voluntary Code of Conduct built around a “watch-out list” of 82 high-risk but unscheduled chemicals, including aniline, propionyl chloride and valerophenone.Releasing it in Ahmedabad on June 16, NCB director-general Anurag Garg was candid about the limits of policing: “While enforcement agencies play a critical role in interdiction and investigation, the fight against synthetic drugs cannot be won through enforcement action alone.”He said the chemicals industry had a crucial role to play, because those closest to the supply chain are often best placed to spot the early signs of diversion: unusually large or suspicious orders, abnormal purchasing or consumption patterns, and attempts to conceal a chemical’s intended end use.Govt is seeking to strengthen that vigilance with technology. The PREP Portal, introduced under its Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), is designed to track dual-use chemicals through India’s supply chains and flag potential diversion before consignments leave the country.For investigators tracking the trade across continents, the devastation caused by illicit fentanyl is no longer in question. The harder question is whether regulation can keep pace with the chemical supply chains that sustain it. India’s chemical corridors are now central to that challenge.
Article Summary: Just 2mg of fentanyl — an amount that can fit on a pencil tip — is enough to kill an adult. Fentanyl has become the leading cause of accidental death among americans aged 18 to 44. For years, mexican cartels sourced many of its precursor chemicals through china.

Article Title: Trump's voter ID praise follows Gyanesh Kumar - Sergio Gor meet
Article Text:
In this image posted on Aug. 12, 2026, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor during a meeting at Nirvachan Sadan, in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: US President Donald Trump's post appreciating India's mandatory elector identification system followed an Aug 12 meeting between chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor at Nirvachan Sadan. Kumar apprised the latter that electoral photo identity cards had been issued by EC to nearly 1 billion electors and that the turnout in recent Indian polls was higher than that in major democracies of the world.The query by Kumar that Trump cited in his post had figured in the discussions, which were part of an exercise by CEC to take forward the spirit of Delhi Declaration 2026.TOI learned that Gor was curious about various aspects of Indian elections. Kumar explained how polls were held under the scrutiny of all political parties, represented by booth level agents during the preparation of the electoral roll, polling agents during voting and counting agents on counting day. According to EC officials, electoral rolls are prepared for each of the 1.2 million polling booths by booth level officers who are employees of state govt.Kumar cited the high turnout, particularly in the last round of assembly elections in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry, to highlight the popular perception in their favour.Officials said the recent polls witnessed a turnout of 93.7% in Bengal, 91.2% in Puducherry, 86.3% in Assam, 86% in TN and 79.5% in Kerala. The Bengal turnout was higher than that recorded in 25 of the world's leading democracies, including Australia, Belgium, Indonesia, South Korea, Brazil, Argentina, France, US, UK and Japan.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump's post appreciating india's mandatory elector identification system followed an aug 12 meeting between chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar and us ambassador to india sergio gor at nirvachan sadan. Kumar apprised the latter that electoral photo identity cards had been issued by ec to nearly 1 billion electors.

Article Title: Trump tariffs: India seeks WTO consultations over 50% US duties quota on quartz surface imports
Article Text:
India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the US in FY26.

What the 50% tariff quota for quartz surface products is about

As the Donald Trump administration continues to find ways to impose tariffs, India has approached the World Trade Organization (WTO) seeking consultations with the US over Washington’s tariff-rate quota on imports of quartz surface products. The measure took effect on August 15 and is set to remain in force for four years.India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the US in FY26. The US has identified India, Vietnam, Spain and Thailand as major exporters of these products.US President Donald Trump issued a proclamation on July 31 introducing a tariff-rate quota of up to 50% on quartz surface product imports from several countries.Also Read | 100% tariffs: Why India may ignore Trump threat and continue buying Russian crude oil The move came after the US International Trade Commission said that imports of these products had risen sufficiently to become a substantial cause of serious injury to US producers of similar or directly competing products.In its August 14 communication to the WTO, New Delhi said it has a "substantial interest" in the matter and suggested that the consultations be conducted virtually at a time mutually convenient to both sides, according to an ET report."India would like to propose that the consultations mentioned above take place virtually as per mutual convenience of both sides," India told the WTO while requesting consultations under the WTO agreement on safeguards.This is the fourth instance in which India has sought such consultations with Washington. Earlier cases involved steel and aluminium, automobiles and auto components, and copper imports.WTO rules provide an exemption from safeguard measures for developing countries whose individual share of the relevant imports is below 3%, provided that the combined share of all such developing countries does not cross 9% of total imports.Washington has imposed a 10% tariff on Indian goods following a Section 301 investigation into forced labour and is also moving ahead with legislation that could impose tariffs of as much as 100% on India and four other countries identified as major buyers of Russian oil and gas. At the same time, India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a trade agreement.The US last week also included India among more than 40 countries that it identified as part of a "shadow trans-shipment network", alleging that the network enables Chinese goods to enter the US while avoiding tariffs. Washington has said it plans to use artificial intelligence to detect and take action against such shipments.Also Read | Beijing’s billion-barrel weapon: Why India must prepare for China-driven oil prices
Article Summary: Us president donald trump issued a proclamation on july 31 introducing a tariff-rate quota of up to 50% on quartz surface product imports from several countries. The measure took effect on august 15 and is set to remain in force for four years. India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the us in fy26.

Article Title: 'Every voter had valid photo ID': Trump cites Indian election system to make case for 'Save America Act'
Article Text:
Trump praises India’s election system, pushes SAVE America Act

What is Save America Act

Require voters to show valid ID before registering.

Require proof of US citizenship.

Restrict mail-in voting, with exceptions for illness, disability, military service or travel.

Require states to remove non-citizens from voter rolls.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised India’s election system and called for the passage of the SAVE America Act, which seeks to require proof of citizenship and voter identification in US elections.In a post on Truth Social, Trump cited a recent conversation involving Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and highlighted India’s use of photo identification for voters.Trump said, "Earlier this month, India’s Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, asked our Administration, How can you have Elections in the US without a valid Photo ID?"Referring to the last general election, Trump said, "India's last Election had 646,000,000 Voters! Less than 1 per cent voted by mail, and every single Voter had to have a VALID Photo Identity Document."Trump also renewed his call for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, saying, "We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now!"According to the White House, the proposed legislation seeks to ensure that only US citizens are eligible to vote in federal elections. "American citizens and only American citizens should decide American elections," the White House said, describing the bill as a "common sense, bipartisan bill."The legislation would require voters to provide valid identification and proof of US citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections. It also proposes limiting mail-in voting to certain circumstances, including illness, disability, military service and travel, according to news agency ANI.The White House said the bill would further require states to remove non-citizens from federal voter rolls. "If you want to register to vote in the United States, you have to be a citizen in the United States," it said.The administration also compared US election practices with those of other countries, arguing that the US has weaker voter-identification safeguards. "India and Brazil tie voter ID to a biometric database, while the United States largely relies on self-attestation for citizenship," the White House said.The bill was introduced in Congress on January 29. Trump has repeatedly backed the SAVE America Act, arguing that stricter voter-ID and citizenship requirements are necessary to strengthen election security.The SAVE America Act is a proposed US law aimed at tightening voting rules in federal elections. It would:MAGA supremo Donald Trump has urged both Republicans and Democrats to support the bill, arguing that only US citizens should decide US elections.The bill also compares US election rules with those in other countries. It says India and Brazil link voter IDs to biometric databases, while the US largely relies on self-attestation of citizenship. It also points to stricter ballot and mail-voting rules in countries such as Germany, Canada, Denmark and Sweden.
Article Summary: Trump praises india’s election system, pushes save america act. Bill would require voters to show valid id before registering. Require proof of us citizenship. Restrict mail-in voting, with exceptions for illness, disability, military service or travel.

Article Title: 'Not a single protester died': Rijiju defends Delhi police response to Jantar Mantar protests
Article Text:
Rijiju defends police response to student protests (ANI image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday defended the Bihar and Delhi governments and law enforcement agencies over their handling of student protests, saying security forces managed large crowds without any casualties or serious injuries."Not a single person died; not a single person suffered a broken bone. Not even one protester is in the hospital with a serious injury. Consider the scale of this movement: thousands turned up, and so many criminals infiltrated under the guise of students," he said as cited by news agency ANI.Rijiju praised the police and administration for their handling of the protests, while contrasting it with the response to demonstrations under previous Congress-led governments."If such a movement had taken place during the Congress era, and many did, resulting in thousands of deaths, one should praise the Delhi police and the administration for handling such a massive protest without allowing even a single serious injury. Thousands actually died from gunfire during the Congress era," Rijiju said."It is the Congress that imposes an Emergency in response to protests. You might recall how many people have fallen victim to gunfire during the various movements that have taken place in this country.Even during the movement to create the state of Telangana, so many people were killed... In this movement, not a single shot was fired," he added.Rijiju said that despite the presence of thousands of protesters, including what he described as political agitators from the Aam Aadmi Party, Bhim Army and Samajwadi Party, as well as “dafli-playing agitators”, the Delhi Police used minimal force. He said force was used only when demonstrators attempted to break through barricades and march towards Parliament."Furthermore, more than half the people, whether from the Aam Aadmi Party, the dafli-playing agitators, the Bhim Army, or the Samajwadi Party, came and incited others to violence; yet, not a single casualty occurred," Rijiju added.On the Gen-Z movement and its demand for education reforms, Rijiju said the Narendra Modi-led NDA government remained committed to the welfare of the country’s youth.He also called for strict judicial action against those responsible for examination leaks and reiterated the government’s zero-tolerance stance on violence during public protests."We respect the students' sentiments. The Prime Minister introduced such a good law and took step after step, promising to work for their future," Rijiju said.The remarks came amid student protests in Bihar over alleged examination irregularities and the NEET paper leak controversy.Clashes were reported between protesters and police in Siwan on July 25 following stone-pelting, after which police used tear gas and lathi charges to disperse the crowd. An AK-47 firing incident was also reported during the unrest.The remarks come weeks after the CJP called off its 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar on July 25, following the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and assurances on some of the protesters’ other demands.The agitation was centred on the NEET paper leak issue and drew students and young volunteers from across the country, along with support from opposition leaders. Activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest on June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike. He was later shifted to Safdarjung Hospital after his health deteriorated.The protest also saw police action on July 20 when demonstrators attempted to march towards Parliament. The Congress and other opposition parties later raised the issue in Parliament, contributing to disruptions during proceedings.
Article Summary: Union parliamentary affairs minister kiren rijiju defends police response to student protests. He says security forces managed large crowds without any casualties or serious injuries. Comments come amid student protests in bihar over alleged examination irregularities and the neet paper leak controversy.

Article Title: Army chief Seth meets Nepal PM Shah, discusses defence ties amid border tensions
Article Text:
Army chief General Seth with Nepal PM Balendra Shah

General Seth conferred honorary Nepali Army general rank

Visit comes amid India-Nepal unease

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Army chief general Dhiraj Seth met Nepal prime minister and defence minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu on Tuesday, with the two sides discussing bilateral issues and ways to strengthen military ties amid a period of unease in relations between the two neighbours.General Seth, who is on a four-day visit to Nepal at the invitation of Nepali Army chief general Ashok Raj Sigdel, held the meeting at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers in Singha Durbar.Indian Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava was also present. According to sources at the Prime Minister's secretariat, the discussions focused on matters of mutual interest and strengthening bilateral military relations.The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu said General Seth called on the Prime Minister and held "warm and productive" discussions on strengthening defence cooperation between both countries. General Seth also visited the Nepali Army Command and Staff College in Shivapuri, where he shared his perspectives on professional military education and contemporary security challenges with faculty and student officers.The visit comes as India and Nepal continue a unique military tradition dating back to 1950.Under the arrangement, the army chiefs of the two countries are conferred the honorary rank of general in each other's armies as a symbol of their longstanding defence ties.Nepal President Ramchandra Paudel conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army on General Seth during a ceremony in Kathmandu on Monday.General Seth had earlier held bilateral talks with General Sigdel at Nepal Army headquarters, where the two discussed matters of mutual interest.The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu said the army chief's visit “reaffirms the unique and time-tested defence relations between India and Nepal”, describing the ties as being rooted in shared values, mutual trust and enduring military-to-military relations.Gen Seth's visit comes against the backdrop of some strain in India-Nepal ties, particularly over the longstanding border dispute involving Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura and Kalapani. India maintains that the territories are part of Uttarakhand, while Nepal has claimed them as part of its territory.Shah had said in Parliament in May that Kathmandu was discussing the border issue not only with India but also with China and the UK. New Delhi subsequently rejected any role for third parties in resolving the boundary dispute.Despite these differences, Shah has recently signalled a push to deepen ties with New Delhi. Earlier this month, he held his first one-on-one meeting with Indian Ambassador Srivastava and stressed the importance of Nepal's “historic relationship” with India.Shah has not yet visited either India or China since becoming prime minister. Instead, Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal travelled to both New Delhi and Beijing in June.The visit by Gen. Seth also comes after Shah's predecessor, K P Sharma Oli, made China his first foreign destination after taking office in 2024, departing from the longstanding practice of Nepalese prime ministers making India their first foreign visit.During his Nepal visit, General Seth also offered prayers at Kathmandu's Pashupatinath Temple.
Article Summary: General seth is on a four-day visit to nepal at the invitation of nepali army chief general ashok raj sigdel. The indian embassy in kathmandu said general seth held "warm and productive" discussions on strengthening defence cooperation between both countries.

Article Title: 'Credibility well established globally': MEA on Trump's praise for CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:

Article Title: Nepal: Break Agniveer hiring deadlock, Gorkha veterans press Balen government
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Calls for Nepal to allow its citizens to join the Indian Army under its Agnipath scheme have grown louder ahead of Army chief General Dhiraj Seth's scheduled participation in an ex-servicemen rally for Gorkha veterans in Pokhara Wednesday, bringing the stalled recruitment issue back into focus during his three-day visit.Days before Gen Seth's arrival, hundreds of former Indian Army personnel, their families, and Gorkha aspirants marched in Pokhara, urging Nepal PM Balen Shah to allow recruitment under Agnipath. They submitted a memorandum to Shah and home minister Sudan Gurung.The deadlock has remained an unresolved backdrop to Gen Seth's visit, though official accounts of his talks with Nepal Army chief General Ashok Raj Sigdel have made no mention of the issue. Gen Seth was conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepal Army by President Ramchandra Paudel Monday. Gen Seth met Shah in Kathmandu Tuesday, but Agnipath found no public mention in the official statement.Colonel Krishna Bahadur Khatri (retd) told TOI from Kathmandu that Nepal's stand had "deprived its youths of an opportunity still seen by many Gorkha families as far better than low-paid employment overseas".Captain Rudra Thapa (retd) said the freeze had pushed many young men towards low-paid, physically demanding jobs in the Gulf and other countries when they could have earned a far income through military service. "If they were allowed to join Indian Army as Agniveers, they could have earned around Nepalese Rs 45-50 lakh, including benefits, in four years," Thapa said."If govt does not allow recruitment into foreign armies, it must be able to provide employment at home."India introduced Agnipath in June 2022, under which recruits serve for four years and up to 25% may later be absorbed into regular service. Nepal declined to allow recruitment under the new terms, arguing that the four-year contractual model marked a departure from the long-term service and pension arrangement that underpinned the 1947 tripartite agreement. No Nepal-domiciled Gorkhas have been recruited since.
Article Summary: Nepal refuses to allow its citizens to join the indian army under its agnipath scheme. Army chief general dhiraj seth is scheduled to participate in an ex-servicemen rally for gorkha veterans in pokhara wednesday. Hundreds of former indian army personnel, their families, and gorkha aspirants have marched urging nepal pm balen shah to allow recruitment.

Article Title: Search ops launched in parts of J&K after reports of suspicious movements
Article Text: JAMMU: Security forces launched search operations following reports of the movement of terror suspects in Udhampur, Reasi and Kathua districts of Jammu & Kashmir, officials said on Tuesday.A man from Udhampur’s Talot village reported to the local police that some suspected individuals knocked on his door late Monday and asked for food.When locals did not respond to the repeated knocks for several minutes and then alerted the security forces, the suspects left the area towards higher reaches of Khuban in the district.The searches come just a week after a video purportedly showing four suspected terrorists moving near Ramtund Peak in Doda district surfaced, prompting security forces to launch a massive search operation on Aug 11.
Article Summary: A man from udhampur’s talot village reported to the local police that some suspected individuals knocked on his door late monday and asked for food. When locals did not respond to the repeated knocks for several minutes and then alerted the security forces, the suspects left.

Article Title: BRICS nations oppose EU carbon border tax at the group's environment ministers’ meeting
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BRICS nations, including India, China, Russia, South Africa, Brazil and others, on Tuesday opposed the European Union’s carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) and any other such trade barriers, calling them “unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist measures”.CBAM, which entered its operational regime on January 1, is a tool to put a price, through imposing a border tax, on carbon-intensive goods, like iron and steel, aluminium and cement, that are entering the 27 EU nations.India opposed the proposal from the time it was conceived, arguing that the unilateral move placed an additional burden on businesses in developing economies due to embedded emissions in their products.“We oppose unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist measures that are not in line with international law, such as CBAM, and express concern that such measures undermine efforts by countries, specifically the developing countries, aimed at addressing the adverse impacts of climate change, increasing adaptive capacity and resilience,” said BRICS nations’ joint ministerial statement (JMS) adopted unanimously at the conclusion of the group’s 12th environment ministers’ meeting here.Delivering his keynote address at the meeting, held under India’s BRICS chairship 2026, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav highlighted the growing global environmental challenges of climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution and disaster risks, and called for stronger cooperation among 11 member countries of the group on forest fire prevention, preparedness, early warning, response and post-fire recovery.The meeting unveiled four knowledge compendiums prepared by the BRICS Environment Working Group, reflecting leading practices, knowledge systems and innovations among the member countries.The countries also adopted four outcome documents, including terms of reference for a network of BRICS institutions to advance knowledge sharing, research and innovation in sustainable lifestyles, and integrated landscape management for combating desertification.Besides Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, other members of the group are Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, UAE and Saudi Arabia. These countries, put together, account for 40% of global GDP. Ministers or heads of delegations of all member countries, except Saudi Arabia, attended the ministerial meeting.
Article Summary: India, china, russia, south africa, brazil and others opposed the european union’s carbon border adjustment mechanism. Cbam is a tool to put a price, through imposing a border tax, on carbon-intensive goods. India opposed the proposal from the time it was conceived.

Article Title: Evening news wrap: Pak SC directs govt to shift Imran to hospital; blast near Kabul school injures around 50 children, and more
Article Text:
Pakistan SC directs govt to move Imran Khan, while a grenade blast near Kabul school injures around 50 children. Meanwhile, Bihar transfers 17 IPS officers amid row over student protest (Photo: AP/IANS)

Article Title: 'Please take Gyanesh Kumar to America': Congress's jibe at CEC after Trump lauds Indian electoral system

Congress MP and spokesperson Pawan Khera on Tuesday took a dig at chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after US President Donald Trump cited India’s election system while calling for stricter voter identification rules in the United States.In his post on X, Khera said, “Please take Gyanesh Kumar Gupta to America. Article Title: “I had the ability to forgive”: How Baker Mayfield chose forgiveness to reopen the door with his family after $11.741M dispute
Article Text:
How Baker Mayfield chose forgiveness to reopen the door with his family after $11.741M dispute(Getty Images)

How did Baker Mayfield choose forgiveness after the $11.741 million family dispute?

How did Kova help Baker Mayfield rebuild his family relationship?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Baker Mayfield has found a way forward in one of the hardest chapters of his life. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is rebuilding ties with his family after a financial dispute involving $11.741 million. His daughter Kova helped create a new opening. Now, Mayfield says forgiveness has allowed him to look beyond a painful family fight and focus on what comes next.The dispute dates back to 2018, when money belonging to Baker Mayfield, Emily Mayfield and their company allegedly moved to businesses connected to Baker’s father and brother. The case later reached court before Mayfield sought a different path with his family.The conflict began between 2018 and 2021, when Baker Mayfield and Emily Mayfield alleged that about $12 million from their accounts and Team BRM moved to companies connected to Baker Mayfield’s father, James W. Mayfield, and brother, Matt Mayfield. The Mayfields claimed they did not authorize the transfers and did not receive an equity interest in the company.The issue became more serious in August 2023, when Baker Mayfield and Emily Mayfield sought financial records connected to the companies.The two sides later reached a confidential settlement that became effective on January 23, 2024. Under that agreement, Camwood Capital agreed to repay $11.741 million plus interest.But the settlement did not close the chapter. On Nov. 22, 2024, Baker Mayfield, Emily Mayfield and Team BRM filed another lawsuit. They alleged that Camwood Capital had not made the required payments or fulfilled other terms of the settlement.That history makes Baker Mayfield’s latest comments much more meaningful. Despite everything that happened, the Buccaneers quarterback has decided not to let the dispute permanently define his relationship with his family.In an interview with the Tampa Bay Times, Baker Mayfield explained how his daughter Kova helped change the situation. He recalled taking Kova to meet his family around her first birthday and described the emotional effect of that meeting.“It's been good. Also, for them to have two grandbabies, it's tough. What's in the past is in the past. Emily and I took (daughter Kova) down right around her first birthday. First time they met her, and you (could) tell it just melted them.He further added, “You can't put yourself on a pedestal and act like I haven't made mistakes in my life. I had the ability to forgive and that was what I wanted to get across. But we're here, and the door is open.”The quote explains the change better than any legal document could. Baker Mayfield did not say the dispute never happened. Instead, he accepted that the past existed while choosing to make room for his family again.Kova’s meeting with Baker Mayfield’s family gave everyone something new to focus on. Mayfield said having two grandchildren made the situation harder to keep apart, especially after the family finally met his daughter.That moment also gave Baker Mayfield a chance to approach the relationship differently. He acknowledged his own mistakes and chose forgiveness instead of continuing the conflict.For the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback, that does not erase the $11.741 million legal battle. It simply separates the financial dispute from his hopes for his family.The legal fight may remain part of Baker Mayfield’s history, but his latest comments show that he does not want it to control his family’s future. His message is clear: the past stays in the past, while the door to reconciliation remains open.
Article Summary: Tampa bay buccaneers quarterback is rebuilding ties with his family after a financial dispute involving $11.741 million. The dispute dates back to 2018, when money belonging to baker mayfield, emily mayfield and their company allegedly moved to businesses connected to baker’s father and brother.

Article Title: ‘All trade, commercial exchanges halted’: How UAE responded to Iran’s latest ballistic missile attack
Article Text:
A view of the Dubai city skyline. (AP Photo)

UAE freezes economic ties with Tehran

Iran denies launching missiles

Missile attack threatens fragile UAE-Iran thaw

Strait of Hormuz tensions add to pressure

Trump tensions with Oman over Iran deal

Iran says Strait will not reopen yet

The United Arab Emirates has suspended all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran after accusing Tehran of launching two ballistic missiles towards the Gulf state, dealing a fresh blow to efforts to ease tensions between the two countries.The UAE defence ministry said its air-defence systems detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran towards its territory on Tuesday. The incident triggered an emergency alert on residents' phones and was described as the first direct Iranian attack on the UAE since May.The ministry later said its assessment indicated that the missiles had been targeting maritime traffic. One missile fell into the sea outside the UAE's territorial waters, while the other fell within them. No damage or injuries were reported.Following the missile incident, the UAE foreign affairs ministry announced that it was halting economic engagement with Iran until further notice.The ministry said that “in light of regional escalations that undermine regional and international peace and security, all trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran have been halted until further notice”.The decision threatens to reverse a gradual restoration of economic and diplomatic links between Abu Dhabi and Tehran. Trade between the UAE and Iranian ports had resumed in some areas, while certain Iranian flights to the UAE had also quietly returned.The emergency alert issued on Tuesday was the first such warning in several months, apart from a false alert in June. Dubai's financial district had also begun filling up with bankers, while Emirati authorities had started allowing some 20,000 Iranian residents who were outside the country when the war began to return to the UAE.Iran has denied the UAE's accusation, with Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei rejecting the claim and warning that such allegations could undermine regional efforts to rebuild trust.Baghaei “completely rejected” the UAE's claim and expressed regret over the accusations against Iran, according to a statement issued by the Iranian Foreign Ministry.“This behaviour is contrary to the principle of good neighbourliness and disrupts ongoing efforts to strengthen trust between regional countries and prevent the escalation of insecurity in the region,” Baghaei said.The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson also called on regional countries to refrain from making “baseless accusations” against Tehran.“The Foreign Ministry spokesman called on all regional parties to refrain from making baseless accusations against the Islamic Republic of Iran, considering the existing complexities due to the ongoing evils of the US and the Zionist regime against regional peace and security, especially the history of numerous false flag operations,” he said.The UAE defence ministry, meanwhile, maintained that its air-defence systems had detected the missiles.“The first fell outside the country's territorial waters, while the second fell within its territorial waters,” the UAE Ministry of Defence said in a post on X.The UAE military said its forces remained on high alert and were prepared to respond to threats against the country's security and sovereignty.The latest confrontation comes after more than two months of efforts by Abu Dhabi and Tehran to reduce tensions that had escalated following the US and Israeli war against Iran that began on February 28.During the conflict, Iran launched repeated missile and drone attacks against neighbouring Gulf states, including the UAE, accusing them of enabling US and Israeli military operations.The UAE was among the Gulf states most heavily targeted, sustaining almost 3,000 missile and drone attacks. Abu Dhabi also carried out scores of strikes against Iran, taking a more hawkish position towards Tehran than several of its Gulf neighbours.Tensions later eased after Washington and Tehran reached a memorandum of understanding in June. However, the agreement began to unravel in early July, after which Iran shifted much of its military focus towards Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan.In recent months, the UAE had sought to rebuild diplomatic and economic channels with Iran while maintaining close military ties with Israel and the United States. Emirati officials have repeatedly said they want to avoid being drawn further into a wider regional conflict.That balancing act is now under growing pressure following the latest missile incident.The confrontation also comes amid escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route for global oil and natural gas shipments.The UAE accused Iran earlier this month of attacking ships operated by Abu Dhabi National Oil Company in the strategic waterway. Tehran has also maintained restrictions on traffic through the strait while issuing increasingly aggressive military rhetoric.A separate maritime incident was reported on Tuesday when an unidentified projectile struck a ship as it sailed out of the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Oman. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre said the strike damaged the vessel's engine room and caused a casualty, while the Omani Coast Guard assisted other crew members.Another cargo vessel was struck by multiple projectiles about 40 nautical miles, or 74 kilometres, southeast of Mokha in Yemen and was declared a “constructive total loss”, according to the British maritime monitoring agency. The agency did not identify the projectiles or those responsible.The incidents have added to concerns over the safety of commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Red Sea region, both vital routes for global trade.The maritime crisis has also drawn Oman into a dispute between Washington and Tehran over arrangements for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.US President Donald Trump threatened Oman after becoming dissatisfied with an emerging agreement between Muscat and Tehran aimed at managing ship traffic through the strategic waterway, according to two regional officials cited by The Associated Press.The officials said the Trump administration objected to parts of the proposed agreement, including joint Iranian and Omani management of the exit route from the strait and voluntary fees on vessels linked to security and maritime environmental protection.Trump on Monday threatened to bomb Oman as it worked with Iran on an agreement intended to reopen the strait and potentially allow Washington and Tehran to resume negotiations aimed at ending the conflict.He later posted a map on social media depicting the Strait of Hormuz as US territory. Trump had previously floated the idea during an Oval Office exchange, saying, “I like the idea of declaring it a territory,” without providing further details.The White House referred to Trump's earlier Oval Office remarks when asked about the latest comments and declined to provide additional details.Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi responded to Trump's remarks on social media.“Just as Trump correctly wrote the name of the eternal Persian Gulf, his delusion regarding the Strait of Hormuz will soon either be corrected, or we will correct this deluded man’s delusions for him,” Gharibabadi wrote on X.Trump has previously threatened Oman over its dealings with Iran. In May, he told reporters during a Cabinet meeting that Oman “will behave just like everybody else, or we will have to blow them up.”Iran has maintained that the Strait of Hormuz will not fully reopen until Washington meets its conditions, including commitments related to sanctions, frozen assets and military operations.“Until the United States fulfills its commitments under the agreement, including lifting the blockade, releasing frozen assets, lifting oil sanctions, ending threats and military operations on all fronts, and implementing the other conditions to which it committed, the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen,” Iranian parliamentary speaker and former US-Iran negotiator Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said.Trump, however, said on Tuesday that the United States had no planned talks with Iran and insisted that the strait was “open and operating”, despite limited maritime traffic and reports of fresh attacks.He also said the US blockade of the waterway remained “in full force and effect” and claimed that all water mines had been removed.Egypt has backed the Iranian-Omani negotiations, saying an agreement could help create conditions for Washington and Tehran to return to talks.The Egyptian foreign ministry said the agreement could pave the way for a “comprehensive and permanent deal that addresses all concerns and enhances regional security and stability."The latest developments leave the UAE facing renewed security pressure as its decision to suspend economic ties with Iran threatens to derail a fragile diplomatic thaw, while tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and wider regional military activity continue to intensify.
Article Summary: Uae accuses tehran of launching two ballistic missiles towards the gulf state. Incident triggered an emergency alert on residents' phones and was described as the first direct iranian attack on the uae since may. The uae foreign affairs ministry announced that it was halting economic engagement with iran until further notice.

Article Title: 'Ready to deal with any threats': UAE vows response after Iran fires two missiles
Article Text:
The missile launches came as efforts continued to reach an agreement between Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

The United Arab Emirates’ defence ministry said on Tuesday that it had detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran towards the Gulf country, as tensions continued to rise across the region.The ministry said both missiles fell into water, with one landing outside the UAE’s territorial waters and the other inside them. It said the country remained prepared to respond to any threats.“The Ministry of Defence confirms that it is on high alert and fully prepared to deal with any threats, and to firmly confront anything aimed at undermining the security of the state, thereby ensuring the preservation of its sovereignty, security and stability, and protecting its interests and national capabilities,” it added.The ministry said that it is 'ready to deal with any threats.'The missile launches came as efforts continued to reach an agreement between Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global shipping. US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the US had no talks planned with Iran, while insisting the strait remained “open and operating” despite sharply reduced traffic.Trump also said the US blockade of Iranian ports remained “in full force and effect” and claimed that all water mines had been removed.He posted a map depicting the Strait of Hormuz as US territory.Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi responded on X, saying: “Just as Trump correctly wrote the name of the eternal Persian Gulf, soon his delusion regarding the Strait of Hormuz will either be corrected or we will correct the delusions of this deluded man," he wrote on X.Shipping data platform Kpler said confirmed crossings through the Strait of Hormuz fell 19.5% last week to 95, with only three vessels passing through on Sunday. No vessels used the Omani routes.Meanwhile, an unidentified projectile damaged the engine room of a ship near Oman, causing “a crew casualty”, according to the British military’s UK Maritime Trade Operations centre. The Omani Coast Guard was assisting the crew, while authorities investigated.Separately, Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed they had launched drones at an oil refinery operated by Saudi Aramco in Saudi Arabia. There were no immediate reports of damage.
Article Summary: The united arab emirates’ defence ministry said on tuesday that it had detected two ballistic missiles launched from iran. The ministry said both missiles fell into water, with one landing outside the uae’s territorial waters and the other inside them. It said the country remained prepared to respond to any threats.

Article Title: Trump’s new election guru? India
Article Text:
Trump cited remarks by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar questioning how Americans can conduct elections without requiring photo identification (Photo: Reuters)

TOI correspondent from Washington:

United States President Donald Trump has apparently discovered the solution to America’s notoriously fickle and complicated election system: Ask India.In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump cited purported remarks by India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar questioning how Americans can conduct elections without requiring photo identification. Trump noted that about 646 million Indians voted in the last general election, with less than 1 per cent voting by mail, and every voter was required to have valid identification to argue: “We need to pass THE SAVE AMERICA ACT, now!” US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor promptly agreed with Trump in a follow-up post.The hotly-contested Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, or SAVE Act, would require documentary proof of US citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections and establish national photo-ID requirements. It has passed the Republican-controlled House of Representatives but repeatedly stalled in the Senate, where Republicans lack the 60 votes to overcome the filibuster. Even some Republicans have baulked at pushing it through without broader support.MAGA principals say the measure is simple: only citizens should vote, and the government should verify that they are citizens. Democrats and voting-rights groups counter that federal law already prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections, documented cases of noncitizen voting are exceedingly rare, and MAGA fear-mongering that millions of non-citizens are voting have been repeatedly disproven.That has produced an inevitable political fracas: critics believe the law's practical effect would be to disproportionally disenfranchise poor, minority, elderly and other voters – which they say is the MAGA game plan – because these groups tend to vote Democratic.So while Republicans call that accusation partisan scaremongering, opponents call it voter suppression dressed up as election security. They argue that the bill creates paperwork barriers for legitimate voters who may lack passports, birth certificates or other acceptable documents, or whose names differ between documents.According to the Brennan Center for Justice, a non-partisan policy institute, more than 21 million voting-age Americans do not have ready access to a passport, birth certificate or naturalization papers. Millions more possess citizenship documents whose names may not match their current legal names. Married women who changed their surnames are one obvious example.Even otherwise, the legislation has become much more than a debate about an ID card; It is also a debate about who should run American elections. And this where Trump's India analogy gets interesting.India has a centralized Election Commission of India which administers national parliamentary and state-assembly elections with standardized procedures and voter identification. America deliberately went in the opposite direction. The Founding Fathers were suspicious of concentrating political power in the federal government, so the US Constitution left substantial responsibility for conducting elections with the states, while giving Congress power to regulate federal elections.So while Congress has enacted national election laws, including voter-registration and election-administration requirements, the day-to-day machinery remains overwhelmingly decentralized. Thus America ended up with thousands of election jurisdictions, varying registration procedures, differing ID requirements, different early- and mail-voting rules.And this constitutional architecture was designed when there were 13 states, not 50, and when the word “instantaneous” would have been considered an ambitious description of horse drawn carriages which plowed through snow in winter to ferry ballot boxes and officials (which is why US elections takes place on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November, but a new President takes oath almost ten weeks later on January 20 after a laborious process).The US system has plenty of weaknesses: registration errors, voter-roll disputes, gerrymandering, unequal procedures, campaign-finance problems, partisan election administration and endless arguments over mail ballots and voting machines. India's system isn't perfect either. Its elections face controversies over money and political influence, voter rolls, and persistent disputes over electronic voting machines.So while neither country has perfect elections, Trump appears to have concluded that America's complicated old electoral jalopy needs an Indian owner's manual, which itself is far from perfect.
Article Summary: Trump cited remarks by india’s chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar questioning how americans can conduct elections without requiring photo identification. Trump noted that about 646 million indians voted in the last general election, with less than 1 per cent voting by mail, and every voter was required to have valid identification.

Article Title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
Article Text:
All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.​

Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy in Mastung district on Friday, injuring six people, including three police personnel.The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said."Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said.All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition. They were taken to a hospital in Quetta for treatment.The attack has raised fresh security concerns in Khad Kocha, an area that has repeatedly come under attack in recent weeks.According to officials, this was the fourth attack on travellers along the same highway since last month. Insurgents have repeatedly targeted people travelling through the area despite a major security operation carried out following the earlier incidents.Security forces have now sealed off the area and launched a search operation to locate those responsible for the latest attack.The incident adds to the continuing security challenges in Balochistan, where armed insurgent groups have carried out attacks against security forces and civilians.
Article Summary: Balochistan home minister mir ziaullah langove escaped unharmed. Six people, including three police personnel, were injured in the attack. The attack took place in the khad kocha area as langove was travelling from quetta to kalat.

Article Title: Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
Article Text:
Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres.

How Russia is 'exploiting' the Volhynia dispute

The facts may be real, but the narrative can still be manipulated

Ukraine fatigue creates fertile ground for the campaign

Russia is being accused of using a painful chapter in the history of Poland and Ukraine to deepen tensions between the two countries, as Warsaw and Kyiv remain divided over the killings that took place during World War 2.Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging in Poland around the Volhynia massacres, while also using the issue to fuel anger against Ukrainians living in the country.The campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say the aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks.Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki, who is from the political right, responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.Polish deputy digital minister Pawel Olszewski said the disagreement was quickly followed by a surge in Russian messaging across social media and Russian media platforms, including Telegram.Research by the state-backed Polish Institute of International Affairs found that Polish-language anti-Ukrainian content on X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube rose by more than 250% after Zelenskyy's decision.Filip Bryjka of PISM said much of this increase appeared to have been artificially boosted through bots, creating the impression that anti-Ukrainian sentiment was spreading rapidly.Analysts say one reason this type of campaign is difficult to detect is that it does not necessarily depend on completely fabricated information.Instead, genuine events and historical grievances can be repeatedly highlighted and framed in ways that encourage anger towards a particular group."The event is real, but the interpretation is imposed by an external actor," said Wojciech Pokora, an analyst at Info Ops Poland Foundation.Moscow has rejected the accusations. The Russian embassy in Warsaw said Russia does not interfere in relations between other countries."The Russian Federation does not interfere in the relations between other states," the Russian embassy in Warsaw said in an emailed statement, adding that accusations about Russia spreading disinformation to undermine support for Ukraine are baseless.The issue has gained greater importance because Poland remains one of Ukraine's strongest supporters in its war against Russia, but public backing for Ukraine has weakened.An IBRiS poll published last month found that 33.6% of respondents said their attitude towards Ukrainians had worsened following the latest dispute linked to the World War Two killings.Another IBRiS survey found that support for continuing military assistance to Ukraine had fallen to 52%, compared with 78% in 2022.Researchers caution that declining support for Ukraine cannot be blamed entirely on Russian influence.Poland is home to an estimated 1.8 to 1.9 million Ukrainian migrants, while disagreements over grain imports and the unresolved legacy of the Volhynia killings have also contributed to public frustration.Olszewski said the Russian messaging had "fallen on fertile ground".Meanwhile, hostility towards Ukrainians in Poland has reportedly increased, prompting prime minister Donald Tusk to call for an end to xenophobic attacks.The issue could become even more politically significant ahead of Poland's 2027 parliamentary elections. Polling suggests Tusk's pro-European government could struggle to retain power, while support for the far-right has been growing.That makes the Volhynia dispute more than a historical argument. For Poland, it touches on a painful national memory. For Ukraine, it is part of a complicated shared history with its neighbour. And for Russia, Polish analysts argue, the disagreement offers an opportunity to deepen divisions between two countries that have otherwise stood together against Moscow.
Article Summary: Polish officials and researchers say moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the volhynia massacres. Campaign largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in polish. Analysts say aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.
